title: Zero-component zig-zags are boundaries
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a first-quadrant homological double complex of $R$-modules with commuting horizontal and vertical differentials $d$ and $\delta$. Write $T_n(A)$, $Z_n(A)$ and $B_n(A)=\operatorname{im}(D_{n+1})$ for the total module, zig-zag cycle submodule and boundary submodule [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. Assume for every $q\ge0$ and $p\ge1$ that $A_{p+1,q}\xrightarrow{d}A_{p,q}\xrightarrow{d}A_{p-1,q}$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. For $n\ge0$ and $a\in Z_n(A)$ with $a_{0,n}=0$, one has $a\in B_n(A)$.

proof.text: For n=0 the sole component is zero, hence a=0 is a boundary. For n>0 start with k=1, a residual equal to a and accumulated boundary tuple zero. Inductively assume the residual is a cycle with all horizontal indices below k zero and that a equals the residual plus the boundary of the accumulated tuple.

For 1 <= k <= n the cycle equation at (k-1,n-k) gives d(a_(k,n-k))=delta(a_(k-1,n-k+1))=0. Exactness at the positive index k supplies f in A_(k+1,n-k) with d(f)=a_(k,n-k). Subtract the boundary supported at (k+1,n-k), and add this tuple to the accumulated tuple. It kills the kth component and affects only the next component. Boundaries are cycles by the first functoriality clause, so the induction is preserved. At k=n all residual components vanish; direct-sum extensionality and linearity give the required boundary expression.

lean.statement:
theorem zigzag_zero_component_boundary
    (A : HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.down ℕ)
      (ComplexShape.down ℕ))
    (hrow : ∀ (p q : ℕ), 0 < p →
      (ShortComplex.mk ((A.d (p + 1) p).f q) ((A.d p (p - 1)).f q)
        (by rw [← HomologicalComplex.comp_f, A.d_comp_d,
          HomologicalComplex.zero_f])).Exact)
    (n : ℕ) (a : zigzagTotal A n) (ha : a ∈ zigzagCycles A n)
    (hzero : DirectSum.component R (ZigzagIndex n)
      (fun i : ZigzagIndex n => (A.X i.1.1).X i.1.2)
      ⟨(0, n), by simp⟩ a = 0) :
    a ∈ zigzagBoundaries A n
